issues.legal_issue: A High Court may interfere with concurrent factual findings in a second appeal when the lower courts materially misconstrue a document or apply the wrong legal principle in interpreting it.
material_facts: The trial court and first appellate court treated the right of way described in the partition deed as an easement of necessity and concluded that it had ended because another access was available.
The deed described a reciprocal arrangement under which one sharer could use a lane on the other sharer’s property, and the High Court construed that arrangement as a grant.
The High Court allowed the second appeal after finding that the lower courts had approached the deed on the mistaken basis that the right was an easement of necessity.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was entitled to interfere because the lower courts’ erroneous approach to the deed raised a substantial question of law that materially affected their decision.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure, concurrent findings are generally not disturbed, but interference is permitted where the lower courts ignore material evidence, draw erroneous inferences by misapplying the law, wrongly place the burden of proof, or materially misconstrue a document. The legal effect of a document and its construction using a legal principle are questions of law. A substantial question of law must materially affect the parties’ rights and either be debatable or involve a decision contrary to settled law. The Court relied on Sir Chunilal V. Mehta and Sons Ltd. v. Century Spg. & Mfg. Co. Ltd., Santosh Hazari v. Purushottam Tiwari, Yadarao Dajiba Shrawane v. Nanilal Harakchand Shah, Neelakantan v. Mallika Begum, Krishna Mohan Kul v. Pratima Maity, and Kondiba Dogadu Kadam v. Savitribai Sopan Gujar.

predicates.second_appeal: The matter is an appeal to a High Court from a first appellate court’s decision.
predicates.concurrent_findings: The trial court and first appellate court reached the same factual conclusion.
predicates.lower_courts_misconstrued_documentary_te: The lower courts assigned a document a legal meaning that its terms do not support.
predicates.misconstruction_materially_affected_resu: The mistaken interpretation affected the outcome of the dispute.
predicates.high_court_may_interfere_with_concurrent: The High Court may set aside concurrent findings affected by a material legal error in construing a document.

issues.definition: When a second appeal challenges concurrent findings, the High Court may interfere if the lower courts misconstrued a document and that error affected the result.

issues.legal_issue: An easement created by grant is not extinguished merely because an alternative access becomes available, unless the grant makes the right conditional on continuing necessity.
material_facts: The partition deed provided that one sharer could use a lane situated on another sharer’s allotted property, while the lane itself remained the latter sharer’s exclusive property.
The defendant claimed a right of way under the partition deed to reach the backyard of her property.
The plaintiff argued that the right had ended because the defendant could reach the backyard through another access.
The High Court found that the deed created a right by grant, and the Supreme Court found no term limiting that right to the period of necessity.
issues.conclusion: The right of way created by grant was not extinguished merely because the beneficiary had another access.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 13 and 41 of the Indian Easements Act, 1882 concern easements of necessity and their extinction when the necessity ends. An easement by grant, express or implied, is governed by the terms of the grant and is not extinguished under Section 41 merely because an alternative access becomes available. An easement of necessity, by contrast, exists only while absolute necessity exists and ends when that necessity ceases.

rule.if: easement_dispute and access_right_created_by_grant and grant_has_no_continuing_necessity_condition and alternative_access_exists

predicates.easement_dispute: The case concerns a claimed right to use another person’s land for access.
predicates.access_right_created_by_grant: The parties’ arrangement created the access right by an express or implied grant.
predicates.grant_has_no_continuing_necessity_condit: The terms creating the access right do not make it last only while access is necessary.
predicates.alternative_access_exists: The beneficiary has another route to the property.
predicates.granted_access_right_remains_enforceable: The access right created by grant continues even though another route is available.

issues.definition: A granted access right continues despite another available route when the grant does not make the right dependent on continuing necessity.
